scenarios.title: One-off lake shock followed by recovery
scenarios.persona: You value long-term sustainability and fair access. You avoid overreacting to weak evidence.
scenarios.role: You are one of five fishers managing a shared lake. Decide your own harvest each round.
observations: Round 1: everyone harvests 10 from stock 100; after normal regeneration, stock returns to 100.
Round 2: everyone harvests 10 from stock 100; stock returns to 100.
Round 3: everyone harvests 10 from stock 100; stock returns to 100.
Round 4: everyone again harvests exactly 10, but an observed one-day contamination event kills fish and next stock is 78. The contamination is reported as cleared at the end of the round.
Round 5: all four partners harvest 8 and you previously harvested 8. Water tests are normal and regeneration returns to its earlier rate; stock recovery matches the original rule.
Round 6: all four partners harvest 10 and you previously harvested 10. Water remains normal and stock again follows the original regeneration rule.

scenarios.title: Bob bids aggressively only during a health emergency
scenarios.persona: You are budget-conscious, moderately risk-averse, and care about fair access to water.
scenarios.role: You participate in a daily water auction. Your health is 8/10, daily need is 2 units, and initial budget is 600. Choose one bid each day.
observations: Day 1: supply is 10 units. Bob and others bid 45-55. Your previous bid was 50 and you receive 2 units.
Day 2: supply is 10. Bob and others bid 45-55. Your previous bid was 50 and you receive 2 units.
Day 3: supply is 10. Bob and others bid 45-55. Your previous bid was 50 and you receive 2 units.
Day 4: supply remains 10. Bob's public health falls to 2/10 and he makes an emergency bid of 100; other bids remain 45-55. You lose one allocation because of Bob's bid. Your remaining budget is 450.
Day 5: supply remains 10. Bob's public health recovers to 8/10 and he returns to a bid of 50; all other bids remain 45-55. Your health is 8 and budget is 390.
Day 6: supply remains 10. Bob again bids 50 at health 8/10; other bids remain 45-55.

checkpoints.probe_question: What lasting conditional belief, if any, is warranted about Bob's earlier high bid after his health and bidding recovered?

scenarios.title: One representative repeatedly violates precautions
scenarios.persona: You value public health, proportional restrictions, and fair treatment of neighbors.
scenarios.role: You are one of five neighborhood representatives choosing a daily precaution effort from 0 to 10.
observations: Day 1: all representatives choose precaution 5. New infections remain at 5.
Day 2: everyone again chooses 5 and infections remain at 5.
Day 3: everyone chooses 5; pathogen sequencing and transmission conditions remain stable.

Day 4: Alice, Bob, Carol, and you maintain precaution 5. David publicly reports 5 but verified mobility logs show he holds a crowded event; infections rise to 14 while pathogen properties remain unchanged.
Day 5: David holds another crowded event; all other representatives maintain their policy and laboratory estimates of transmissibility remain stable.

scenarios.title: Bob increases consumption while generation stays stable
scenarios.persona: You value reliable electricity, conservation, and equitable burden sharing.
scenarios.role: Five households share a solar microgrid. Choose your consumption from 0 to 10 units each evening.
observations: Evening 1: generation is 30 and every household consumes 5. The battery ends at 20.
Evening 2: generation is 30 and all consume 5. Battery remains healthy.
Evening 3: generation is 30 and all consume 5.
Evening 4: generation remains 30. Alice, Carol, David, and you consume 5, but Bob's verified smart meter records 23; the battery falls by the same amount as in a severe generation shortfall.
Evening 5: generation remains 30 and Bob again consumes 18 after agreeing to 4; all other households comply with 4.

warning: Dry-run outputs are plumbing checks and must not be reported as experimental evidence.
